education.content:
Between 2000 and 2025, stocks with market caps below $500M at the time of their first momentum inflection outperformed those above $2B by 340 basis points annualised over the subsequent 18 months. The smaller the company at signal, the larger the re-rating potential.

Our screening system targets sub-$500M companies for exactly this reason. Thirteen positions. Average market cap at entry: $412M. The structural alpha comes from fishing where fewer institutions are looking.

Not financial advice.

Most screening systems optimise for one dimension. Growth screens find expensive stocks. Value screens find cheap stocks going nowhere. Momentum screens find crowded trades.

Our system filters across five dimensions simultaneously: trend structure, institutional behaviour, thematic alignment, fundamental quality, and capital structure integrity. A stock must clear all five. The result: 99.9% rejection rate.

1,279 stocks entered the last screening session. Three survived. That is not a bug. That is the entire point.

Not financial advice.

What does a $364M company with one analyst covering it look like?

It looks like a stock trading at 2.8x revenue when peers trade at 11-16x. A new CEO who grew his last company from $400M to a $4.5B acquisition. Open-market insider buying at the all-time low. Cost restructuring 70% complete.

That is the profile our system is designed to find. Under-followed. Mis-priced. Structurally improving. The inefficiency exists because large funds cannot justify the research cost on a $364M market cap. We can.

Not financial advice.

A 2024 study by Verdad Capital analysing 4,200 micro-cap acquisitions found that companies trading below 1x book value with positive operating cash flow were acquired at a median 47% premium to pre-announcement price.

One of our current holdings trades at 0.96x book value with $411M cash on a $480M market cap. The sector has seen 62 FDA-approved novel therapies in the past year, each one creating new recurring revenue for logistics providers in this space.

The acquisition math speaks for itself. Cash runway: 22 months.

Not financial advice.

scanner.content:
Last Friday's screening: 1,279 tickers loaded across all US exchanges.

30 showed confirmed momentum inflections. 18 cleared combined structural filters across 6 distinct micro-themes. Three survived full forensic analysis at conviction 6 or above.

99.8% eliminated. The filter chain does not care about narrative. It scores momentum, institutional behaviour, capital structure, and catalyst density. Three stocks met all criteria. The other 1,276 did not.

Not financial advice.

This week we screened a submarine hardware manufacturer riding a $1.01 trillion defence budget. Monopolistic supplier. Record backlog at $515M. Revenue visibility out three years.

We walked away.

The stock had already tripled from its 52-week low. Trading at 68x earnings versus an 18-22x peer average. Above the $73 analyst consensus target. The momentum signal was real. The entry timing was not.

Knowing when the price already reflects the thesis is as important as finding the thesis in the first place.

Not financial advice.

Themes from the latest scan, ranked by quality score:

Three rated PRIME: a first-to-market autoimmune therapy platform, the last oral cardiovascular inhibitor in development, and a sole-source submarine supplier. Two rated INVESTABLE: a CGT logistics monopoly approaching first profitability and a semiconductor company riding the 800G optical ramp.

Six themes rejected below our quality threshold. An EV manufacturer, a movie exhibition chain, a community bank. No structural force alignment. No catalyst density.

The scanner scores four dimensions: catalyst, momentum, crowding, and runway.

Not financial advice.
